intro.caption: Lesson 3-6 — converting measurements within the same system. The Vipers locked the Drift Crew inside the pit garage! Four keypad bolts hold the door shut, and every bolt asks for a unit conversion.

balloons.t: Breaking news from Garage Four! The door just locked us in with four math bolts!
Qualifiers start soon. Let's crack every conversion and roll out!
Bolt 1 wants 48 inches in feet. Easy! 48 times 12 is 576 feet!
A 576-foot wrench? Sure, Beck. Feet are BIGGER than inches, so you need FEWER!

pages.caption: Beck multiplied when he needed to divide. Going to a smaller unit multiplies; going to a larger unit divides.

balloons.t: Stay in one system! Customary with customary, metric with metric. Check unit size first.
Bolt 2 checks the coolant tank and cable length. Both stay inside one system.
Ask every time: am I trading for a smaller unit or a larger one?
Bolt 3 jumps two steps! Gallons to quarts, then quarts to cups.
Even my lunch juice box has more cups than gallons! Let's chain the factors!
Three final codes on the master lock. No guessing—check the unit size!
Customary, metric, and a two-step chain. Let's open this door!
The garage door is up! Drift Crew hits the neon track right on cue!

win.caption: Within one measurement system, conversion factors are exact. Moving to a smaller unit multiplies; moving to a larger unit divides.

gates.title: Gate 1 · Pick the Direction
gates.prompt: Unlock Bolt 1 by fixing Beck's 48-inch conversion and picking the right direction.
hints: Conceptual: a foot is longer than an inch, so 48 inches makes FEWER feet, not more.
Procedural: divide by the unit ratio (12 inches per 1 foot): 48 ÷ 12.

steps: Practice lock: convert 36 inches to feet (1 ft = 12 in).
Feet are larger than inches, so there will be fewer of them: divide by 12.

items.label: 48 inches = ___ feet (1 ft = 12 in)

fb.msg: 576 is 48 × 12. Feet are LARGER than inches, so divide instead of multiplying.
That subtracts 12 from 48. Use the unit ratio 12 : 1 by dividing.
That adds 12 to 48. Unit conversions multiply or divide, never add.

items.fbDefault: Divide 48 inches by 12 inches per foot.

items.q: Which pair stays inside the same measurement system?

options.fb: Feet are customary and meters are metric. That crosses between systems.
Pounds are customary and kilograms are metric.
Quarts are customary and liters are metric.

gates.pass: CLICK! Bolt 1 slides back — 48 inches is 4 feet, not 576!

gates.title: Gate 2 · Tank & Track
gates.prompt: Convert the coolant tank (metric) and the tow strap (customary) to unlock Bolt 2.
hints: Conceptual: check which unit is smaller. More small units fit in the same amount.
Procedural: use 1 L = 1,000 mL (multiply to mL, divide to L) and 1 yd = 3 ft.

steps: Practice: convert 2 liters to milliliters (1 L = 1,000 mL).
Milliliters are smaller than liters, so multiply: 2 × 1,000 = 2,000 mL.

items.label: 5 liters = ___ milliliters (1 L = 1,000 mL)

fb.msg: 1 liter is 1,000 mL, not 100 mL. Multiply 5 by 1,000.
That divided by 1,000. Milliliters are smaller than liters, so there are MORE of them.

items.fbDefault: Multiply 5 liters by 1,000 milliliters per liter.

items.label: 18 feet = ___ yards (1 yd = 3 ft)

fb.msg: 54 is 18 × 3. Yards are LARGER than feet, so divide by 3.
That subtracted 3. Divide 18 feet into groups of 3 feet per yard.

items.fbDefault: Each yard holds 3 feet. Divide 18 by 3.

gates.pass: CLACK! Bolt 2 opens — 5,000 mL of coolant and 6 yards of strap.

gates.title: Gate 3 · Two-Step Chain
gates.prompt: Bolt 3 needs a two-step conversion inside the same system.
hints: Conceptual: convert to the middle unit first, then convert that result to the target unit.
Procedural: 1 gallon = 4 quarts, and 1 quart = 4 cups. Multiply step by step.

worked.q: How many cups are in 1 gallon? (1 gal = 4 qt, 1 qt = 4 cups)

items.label: 3 gallons = ___ cups (1 gal = 4 qt, 1 qt = 4 cups)

fb.msg: 12 is 3 gallons in QUARTS. You still need to convert quarts to cups (× 4).
Check both steps: 3 gal = 12 qt, and 12 qt × 4 cups/qt = 48 cups.

items.fbDefault: First convert 3 gallons to quarts (× 4), then quarts to cups (× 4).

items.q: Lin needs 400 centimeters in meters (1 m = 100 cm). Which operation works?

options.fb: Meters are larger than centimeters, so the number of meters must be smaller than 400.
Unit conversions use multiplying or dividing by the conversion factor, not subtracting.

gates.pass: SNAP! Bolt 3 clears — 48 cups and 4 meters!

gates.title: Boss Gate · Master Keypad
gates.prompt: Three final locks on the master keypad. Watch your unit direction on every one!
hints: Conceptual: larger unit → smaller unit means MORE pieces (multiply). Smaller unit → larger unit means FEWER pieces (divide).
Procedural: use 1 lb = 16 oz, 1 km = 1,000 m, and 1 yd = 3 ft, 1 ft = 12 in.

steps: Practice lock: convert 32 ounces to pounds (1 lb = 16 oz).
Pounds are larger than ounces, so divide: 32 ÷ 16 = 2 pounds.
worked.q: Convert 4,000 meters to kilometers (1 km = 1,000 m).

items.label: Lock 1 · 80 ounces = ___ pounds (1 lb = 16 oz)

fb.msg: 1,280 is 80 × 16. Pounds are larger than ounces, so divide by 16.

items.fbDefault: Divide 80 ounces by 16 ounces per pound.

items.label: Lock 2 · 3.5 kilometers = ___ meters (1 km = 1,000 m)

fb.msg: That multiplied by 100. There are 1,000 meters in 1 kilometer.

items.fbDefault: Meters are smaller than kilometers, so multiply 3.5 × 1,000.

items.label: Lock 3 · 4 yards = ___ inches (1 yd = 3 ft, 1 ft = 12 in)

fb.msg: 12 is 4 yards in FEET. Convert those 12 feet into inches (× 12).
48 is 4 × 12, which converts feet to inches, not yards to inches.

items.fbDefault: First turn 4 yards into feet (4 × 3 = 12 ft), then multiply by 12 inches per foot.

gates.pass: KRAAACK-WHOOSH! The master lock pops and the garage door rolls up!

journal.heading: Lesson 3-6 — what the lock-in taught us
rows: Customary units (in, ft, yd, oz, lb, cup, qt, gal) convert within customary; metric units (cm, m, km, mL, L) convert within metric.
Going to a SMALLER unit gives MORE pieces, so multiply. Going to a LARGER unit gives FEWER pieces, so divide.
To go from gallons to cups or yards to inches, convert to the middle unit first, then convert again.
48 inches is 4 feet, not 576 feet. Never multiply blindly—check whether the new unit is bigger or smaller.
journal.quote: "If your wrench comes out 576 feet long, you multiplied when you should have divided." — Spark

teacher.suggested: Use during or after lesson 3-6 (Convert Measurements within the Same System). Covers unit ratios, deciding whether to multiply or divide based on unit size, customary and metric conversions, and two-step chains.
standards: Use ratio reasoning to convert measurement units within the same system
